test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 19 Mar 2021 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: What is the maximum validity of an ordinance issued by the President of India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**6 months + 6 weeks**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• An ordinance issued by the President of India is a temporary law that has the same force and effect as an act of Parliament.
 
• The President can issue an ordinance only when both houses of Parliament are not in session.
 
• An ordinance ceases to operate if it is not approved by both houses of Parliament within six weeks of their reassembly.
 
• The maximum validity of an ordinance is six months (the maximum gap between two sessions of Parliament) plus six weeks (time allowed for Parliament to ratify the ordinance).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ordinance:**

 
 
• An ordinance is a decree or law promulgated by the President of India on the advice of the Union Cabinet.
 
• It has the same force and effect as an act of Parliament but is temporary in nature.
 
 
 
• **Parliament Sessions:**
 
 
• The Parliament of India conducts its business in three sessions: the Budget Session, the Monsoon Session, and the Winter Session.
 
• The maximum gap between two sessions can be six months.
 
 
 
• **Reassembly of Parliament:**
 
 
• Once both houses of Parliament reassemble, the ordinance must be laid before them.
 
• It must be approved by both houses within six weeks, failing which it will cease to operate.
